observation_summary: The ListPopulation iterator allows modification of the underlying chromosome list, which violates the expected behavior of the iterator (it should be unmodifiable).
reasoning_summary: The bug is that the iterator returned by ListPopulation exposes the internal modifiable list directly. The fix requires changing the implementation of the iterator method to return an unmodifiable wrapper (e.g., Collections.unmodifiableList(chromosomes).iterator()). This is a procedural/algorithmic correction to the method's return logic, not a design-level capability gap or a simple variable initialization error.
evidence_used: The bug report states: 'Calling the iterator method of ListPopulation returns an iterator of the protected modifiable list. Before returning the iterator we should wrap it in an unmodifiable list.'
The test case expects an UnsupportedOperationException when calling iter.remove(), confirming that the iterator should not support modification.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The capability (iterator) exists, but its implementation is incorrect because it exposes internal state. This is a local procedural fix, not a missing class or design capability.

The interface contract is not being violated by the caller; the internal implementation of the iterator method is simply returning the wrong object type (a modifiable iterator instead of an unmodifiable one).
